Definition: a hawk or other bird of prey
BiblicalUsage: The ayit is a bird of prey — the hawk, the kite, the vulture — and Scripture lets it do God's hard work. The fowls came down on Abram's sacrifice and he drove them away, Isaiah says the birds of prey will be left on the mountains, Jeremiah says God's heritage has become a speckled bird of prey, and Ezekiel calls every feathered fowl to the great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even the birds of prey serve God's purposes. Abram driving them from his sacrifice is my picture of guarding what God has given me.
